observations: body L8-L9, L11-L12: the two relations stand in the middle of the page, each on two lines.

body L16-L17: 71° 34′ is the entry for the tenth degree of Pisces in al-Battānī's table of right ascensions counted from the beginning of Capricorn (Part II, p. 61, f. 179,v.). Recomputed with his obliquity 23° 35′, the right ascension of 340° counted from the beginning of Capricorn is 71° 33′ 15″.
body L17: «Schiaparelli» is set in small capitals; the closing bracket is printed heavy.
body L18: «Ḥabash» is letter-spaced; the last t of «supputat» is printed broken, like f.
body L22: a speck stands before «Capricorni»; it is not a sign.

body L18-L31: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXII) add to the note b) on pp. 163-164: al-Khāzinī (f. 151,r.-v.) and Kūshiyār ibn Labbān also give a table of right ascensions counted from the beginning of Capricorn; one of the problems of az-Zarqālī's book on the saphaea is to find the longitude of a star from its right ascension counted from the beginning of Capricorn (the degree with which the star culminates) and its declination, which Steinschneider mistranslated (Études sur Zarkali, Bullettino di bibliografia, t. XVIII, 1885-86, p. 345 = p. 57 of the offprint); Abū Bakr ibn al-Musharraf, apparently of the 9th century of the hijrah (15th Chr.), computed such tables for every minute of the zodiac (Catalogue of the Cairo library, t. V, p. 238, mīqāt nr. 209); Muḥammad al-Akhṣāṣī of Egypt counted from the same point the right ascensions of 112 fixed stars for about 1650 Chr., in his ad-durrah al-muḍī'ah fī 'l-a‘māl ash-shamsiyyah (Cairo catalogue V, 245, mīqāt nr. 60 and 81), tables edited by Edw. Knobel, On a catalogue of stars in the Calendarium of Mohammad Al Achsasi Al Mouakket, Monthly Notices of the R. Astronomical Society, vol. LV, nr. 8, 1895, p. 429.
body L32: the head of the notes on chapter 6, «Ad» and «caput» in small capitals.
body L36: «1479, 5» is printed with a space after the decimal comma (1479.5 metres).
body L38: a speck stands at the foot between «180» and «000»; it is not a sign.

body L36-L40: 1479.5 m are 6.94 philetaerian stadia of 213.048 m, the seven of the text in round figures. At seven stadia to the mile Ptolemy's 180 000 stadia make 25 714 miles, 71 3/7 to the degree; with the metric values of L36-L37, 25 920 miles and 72 to the degree. The 27 000 miles and 75 miles to the degree of L40 answer to 6 2/3 stadia to the mile; kept as printed.
